b.bio: Joseph-Marie-Bruno-Constantin, Baron Kervyn de Lettenhove, born at Saint-Michel-lez-Bruges on 17 August 1817, was a Belgian historian and politician. He sat for Eeklo in the Chamber of Representatives from 1861 and served briefly as minister of the interior in 1870 before resigning over the Decker appointment to the governorship of Limburg. He then devoted himself to historical scholarship: a French-Academy-crowned study of Froissart's chronicles, editions of Commines, Chastellain, Burgundian chronicles, political relations of the Low Countries under Philip II, and a history of Flanders. He was a corresponding member of the Académie des sciences morales et politiques (1864–1891). The shelf label 'Latin Fathers' is misleading: this is a nineteenth-century scholar, not an ancient author.
b.s: The work held here is his historical research on the struggle between Philip the Fair of France and his opponents—arguing from Cistercian charity and scholarship in Flanders against royal usurpation and appealing to papal protection against Philip the Fair—so readers should treat it as modern historiography on a medieval controversy, not as a patristic text.
